task_description: Build crypto-core/blake3.mjs (from-scratch BLAKE3 per the official specification, pure JS arithmetic, no cryptographic library) and crypto-core/blake3.test.mjs (known-answer vectors plus structural checks), then seal a provenance worklog.

components.compression_function: G mixing function (add-rotr32 by 16/12/8/7) over a 16-word 32-bit state, 7 rounds
components.chunking: 1024-byte chunks, each chained across up to 16 64-byte blocks
components.tree: left-complete binary Merkle tree over chunk chaining values, built incrementally with a stack merged on trailing-zero-bits of the running chunk count
components.domain_flags: CHUNK_START=1, CHUNK_END=2, PARENT=4, ROOT=8, KEYED_HASH=16, DERIVE_KEY_CONTEXT=32, DERIVE_KEY_MATERIAL=64
components.iv: same 8 constants as SHA-256's initial hash values
components.xof: arbitrary-length output via re-invoking compress on the fixed root inputs with an increasing output-block counter

test_vector_provenance.retrieval_method: WebFetch tool (goes through an intermediate LLM summarization step, not a byte-exact transfer)

corrupted_fields.defect: 352 hex chars instead of required 262; tail was a verbatim duplicate of input_len=1's derive_key tail
byte-for-byte identical to input_len=1023's keyed_hash (impossible for genuine distinct-input BLAKE3 outputs); did not match the from-spec implementation
byte-for-byte identical to input_len=1023's derive_key; did not match the from-spec implementation

test_vector_provenance.validation_method: Each fetched field was checked for correct hex length and for accidental duplication across distinct input_len cases, then cross-checked against crypto-core/blake3.mjs (written independently from the spec, before this validation pass). Only fields the implementation reproduced exactly were kept; all others were dropped rather than guessed at.

accomplishments: Implemented BLAKE3 from the official specification in pure JS (crypto-core/blake3.mjs): compression function, 7-round message schedule, chunk chaining, Merkle tree, domain flags, IV, keyed hash, derive_key, and XOF
Fetched official test vectors and discovered + isolated 3 corrupted fields introduced by the fetch pipeline's summarization step, rather than trusting them at face value
Cross-validated all fetched vectors against the independently-written implementation, keeping only confirmed-correct fields (87 of 90)
Generated crypto-core/blake3.test.mjs programmatically (JSON.stringify from validated data straight into source) to avoid manual re-transcription errors on ~87 long hex strings
Added 46 structural checks: determinism, XOF prefix consistency, chunk/tree-boundary continuity, key-sensitivity, avalanche
Ran the test suite: 133 pass, 0 fail
Generated Ed25519 identity key and sealed the worklog
test_result: 133 pass, 0 fail (87 official KAT checks + 46 structural checks)
